candidateDecisions.label: Fundamental and theoretical physics of fields, matter and quantum systems
Astronomy, astrophysics and the physical universe

analysis: The plan directly supports climate and Earth-system questions through Earth System Science Tools (modeling, proxies and isotope tracers), Climate Change (forcing, feedbacks and consequences), Earth Observation (remote sensing, spectral signatures and spatial analysis), and environmental biogeochemistry (aqueous and mineral reactions and carbon cycling). Dynamic Earth and hazards support physical Earth processes; coastal and delta study applies that understanding to flooding, salinity and infrastructure. Energy & Sustainability and Renewable System Design add physical and technical applications of the climate theme through generation, storage, and applied system design. The mathematics and computing sequence offers numerical differential-equation methods, linear systems, probability and data models applicable to natural systems. Sustainability Essentials I and II contain meaningful physical topics including mechanics, thermodynamics, waves and spectroscopy; the cumulative theory and laboratory sequence needed for physics is absent. General mathematical tools and basic waves are insufficient for an astronomy option covering celestial mechanics, stellar or galactic systems and observational methods. Fieldwork, spectroscopy exposure, data analysis and a partner project develop empirical skills without providing a cumulative experimental physics or instrumentation pathway. None of these three directions supports a coherent second option. There is no pair to test for distinctness. Optional UCR independent research is outside the degree and does not stand in for Utrecht’s required specialist project.

alignment.rationale: Both develop calculus for quantitative science.
Both develop linear algebra. Utrecht applies it within a physics sequence.
Both extend mathematical problem solving. UCR emphasizes numerical methods for equations and models.
Both develop empirical data analysis. Utrecht also teaches physics measurement and data acquisition.
Both study links between atmosphere, ocean and climate. UCR uses Earth-system models and tracers. Utrecht emphasizes the forces and equations governing circulation.
Utrecht develops classical and relativistic mechanics through a dedicated course.
Utrecht provides a dedicated course in electromagnetism.
Utrecht studies astronomy and optics. UCR introduces waves and spectroscopy in its sustainability gateway.
Utrecht provides a dedicated quantum mechanics course.
Utrecht develops statistical physics and experiments. UCR’s probability course supplies general statistical tools.

Utrecht requires a supervised physics project. Students normally complete the required taught courses and earn at least 90 EC before starting. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Utrecht requires an experimental physics project. UCR includes environmental fieldwork and data analysis.
Utrecht requires a choice between fluid mechanics and structure of matter.
Choose four level-3 courses. Utrecht offers geophysical fluid dynamics, turbulence and other advanced physics topics.
Utrecht reserves 45 EC for profiling electives.
